problems.title: Number of Islands
problems.statement: Given an m x n 2D binary grid grid where '1' represents land and '0' water, return number of islands.
problems.understanding: An island is surrounded by water and formed by connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically.
problems.intuition: Modify grid in-place (grid[r][c] = "0") to eliminate extra visited set storage.
problems.approach:
1. Traverse every cell (r, c) in grid.
  2. If cell is "1", increment island count and start DFS.
  3. In DFS: set cell to "0" (sink island) and recurse 4 directions.

optimal.title: Optimized Code (Python 3)
complexity: Aux Space: O(R × C) recursion call stack

problems.title: Clone Graph
problems.statement: Given reference of node in connected undirected graph, return deep copy (clone) of graph.
problems.understanding: Map original nodes to new cloned node instances using a map/dictionary to handle cycles and shared neighbors.
problems.intuition: BFS iterative cloning with queue and map prevents stack overflow on deep graphs.
problems.approach:
1. If node is None return None.
  2. Create clones dictionary and queue with root node.
  3. While queue: pop current, iterate neighbors, clone unvisited neighbors, push to queue, and link cloned neighbors.

problems.title: Max Area of Island
problems.statement: Return maximum area of an island (number of connected 1s) in a grid.
problems.understanding: Island area is total land cells connected 4-directionally.
problems.intuition: In-place grid modification (grid[r][c] = 0) while summing connected land cells.
problems.approach:
1. Iterate grid cells. When 1 is found, call DFS.
  2. DFS sets current cell to 0 and returns 1 + dfs(up) + dfs(down) + dfs(left) + dfs(right).
  3. Track maximum area returned across all islands.

problems.title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
problems.statement: Find grid coordinates that can flow water to BOTH Pacific Ocean (top/left) and Atlantic Ocean (bottom/right).
problems.understanding: Reverse problem: ask which cells can be reached by starting at ocean borders and flowing UPHILL.

naive.title: Naive Solution
naive.html: For every cell, perform DFS to check if it reaches both oceans.

problems.intuition: Multi-source BFS starting from ocean borders moving uphill.
problems.approach:
1. Start multi-source BFS from Pacific ocean borders into set P.
  2. Start multi-source BFS from Atlantic ocean borders into set A.
  3. Return intersection of sets P & A.
problems.takeaway: Pattern: Reverse the problem (ask which cells can be reached from ocean flowing uphill).

problems.title: Surrounded Regions
problems.statement: Capture all regions surrounded by 'X'. Modify 'O' to 'X' if completely surrounded.
problems.understanding: Any 'O' connected to border boundary CANNOT be captured. All other 'O' cells will be flipped to 'X'.

naive.title: Naive Solution
naive.html: DFS from every 'O' checking if boundary reachable.

problems.intuition: Boundary-first DFS marking boundary-connected 'O's as '#', then flipping remaining 'O' → 'X' and '#' → 'O'.
problems.approach:
1. Run DFS on all 4 borders to mark safe 'O's as '#'.
  2. Traverse grid: convert any remaining 'O' to 'X'.
  3. Restore '#' back to 'O'.

problems.title: Rotting Oranges
problems.statement: Return minimum minutes that must elapse until no cell has a fresh orange. If impossible return -1.
problems.understanding: Multi-source BFS where all rotten oranges start in queue at minute 0 and rot adjacent fresh oranges simultaneously.
problems.intuition: Multi-source BFS starting from all rotten oranges simultaneously.
problems.approach:
1. Enqueue all rotten oranges (val=2), count total fresh oranges (val=1).
  2. While queue and fresh > 0: increment minutes, rot fresh neighbors, push to queue, decrement fresh count.
  3. Return minutes if fresh == 0 else -1.

problems.title: Walls and Gates
problems.statement: Fill each empty room with distance to its nearest gate. Empty room=INF (2147483647), Wall=-1, Gate=0.
problems.understanding: Multi-source BFS starting from all gates simultaneously.
problems.approach:
1. Enqueue all gate positions (0).
  2. While queue: pop (r, c), check 4 neighbors. If neighbor is INF, update distance to rooms[r][c] + 1 and push.

problems.title: Course Schedule
problems.statement: Determine if you can finish all courses given prerequisite dependencies.
problems.understanding: Can finish all courses iff the prerequisite graph has no directed cycle.
problems.approach:
1. Compute indegrees of all vertices.
  2. Enqueue all vertices with 0 indegree.
  3. While queue: pop node, increment completed count, decrement indegrees of neighbors. Push neighbors hitting 0.
  4. Return completed == numCourses.

problems.title: Course Schedule II
problems.statement: Return ordering of courses to finish all. Return empty array if impossible.
problems.understanding: Find valid topological sort ordering of directed graph.
problems.intuition: Kahn's BFS Algorithm returning topological course order array.
problems.approach:
1. Compute indegrees and build graph.
  2. Enqueue 0 indegree nodes into queue.
  3. Pop queue, append to result order, decrement neighbor indegrees. Push neighbors with 0 indegree.
  4. Return result if length matches numCourses else [].

problems.title: Graph Valid Tree
problems.statement: Determine if an undirected graph of n nodes is a valid tree.
problems.understanding: A tree must have exactly n-1 edges and be fully connected with no cycles.
problems.intuition: Union-Find with path compression and rank optimization.
problems.approach:
1. If len(edges) != n-1 return False.
  2. Initialize parent array [0..n-1].
  3. Union endpoints of each edge; if find(a) == find(b), cycle detected → return False.
  4. Return True.

problems.title: Number of Connected Components
problems.statement: Given n nodes and edges list, return number of connected components.
problems.understanding: Start with n components and decrement by 1 on every successful union of disjoint sets.
problems.intuition: Union-Find tracking component count (components -= 1 on successful union).
problems.approach:
1. Initialize parent = list(range(n)) and components = n.
  2. For each edge (a, b), call union. If merged, decrement components.
  3. Return components count.

problems.title: Redundant Connection
problems.statement: Return edge that can be removed so graph becomes a valid tree. If multiple, return edge that appears last in input.
problems.understanding: An edge is redundant if its endpoints are ALREADY connected in the Union-Find structure.

naive.title: Naive Solution
naive.html: DFS cycle check after adding each edge.

problems.approach:
1. Initialize parent = list(range(n + 1)).
  2. Loop edges (u, v). If find(u) == find(v), return [u, v]. Else union(u, v).

problems.title: Word Ladder
problems.statement: Return length of shortest transformation sequence from beginWord to endWord using wordList.
problems.understanding: Unweighted shortest path problem solved via BFS with pattern wildcard matching.

naive.title: Naive Solution
naive.html: Compare all pairs of words for 1-char difference to build graph.

problems.intuition: Group words into pattern dict neighbors['*ot'] = ['hot', 'dot', 'lot'] to reduce edge lookup to O(L^2 × N).
problems.approach:
1. Build wildcard pattern map for wordList.
  2. Queue with (beginWord, 1), visited set with beginWord.
  3. BFS layer-by-layer: for current word, generate patterns, visit unvisited neighbor words, push to queue with dist+1.
